query: If the ticket types that create the heaviest agent workload were reduced, how much would resolution time drop?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: The query targets 'ticket types that create the heaviest agent workload.' This categorization is the ticket-type dimension the query centers on; it is intervenable in the sense that categories could be reduced/rerouted, and it is the named lever.

per_column.name: affected_system
per_column.rationale: The affected system is a common cause of both what type/category a ticket is and how long it takes to resolve; not named in the query. It is however largely collinear with category, weakening its distinctness.

per_column.name: failure_mode
per_column.rationale: The nature of the failure drives both which category/workload bucket a ticket falls in and its resolution difficulty; not named in query.

per_column.name: ticket_complexity_signal
per_column.rationale: Complexity plausibly influences both which ticket types generate heavy workload and resolution time; not named in query. Borderline mediator, but as an intrinsic difficulty it can act as a common cause.

per_column.name: location_scope
per_column.rationale: Scope (individual vs enterprise-wide) affects both ticket type/workload and resolution time; not named in query.

per_column.name: resolver_match
per_column.rationale: Constant (true for all 500 rows); provides no variation and cannot adjust for anything.

per_column.name: recurrence_indicator
per_column.rationale: Whether an issue recurs can be a common cause of both category/workload and resolution time; not named. Near-constant (480 true), so limited practical value.

per_column.name: is_open_unresolved
per_column.rationale: Being open/unresolved is downstream of (a function of) resolution time itself; conditioning on it is a collider/selection risk, not a confounder.

judge.rationale: A plausible treatment (incident_category / ticket type) is present and is intervenable, matching the 'reduce the ticket types that drive workload' lever. Several genuinely un-named confounders (failure_mode, ticket_complexity_signal, location_scope, affected_system) capture common causes of both ticket type and resolution time, which is what the what-if test rewards. However, quality is diminished: many treatment-adjacent columns are highly collinear with category (mediators/redundant), one column (resolver_match) is a useless constant, and is_open_unresolved is a collider that is outcome-derived and should not be conditioned on. The set sets up an interventional framing but the confounder adjustment is only moderately clean.
